# MeedyaDL 1.9.1

A performance-and-correctness hotfix for people with large music libraries. If your output folder has more than a handful of albums in it — especially when downloading whole artists — this one's for you: real-world testing showed 5–25x faster processing per item on a 484-album library.

### What's fixed

- **Downloads no longer needlessly scan your entire music library.** After a download finished, several background steps — synced-lyrics conversion, tagging, audio fingerprinting, and loudness analysis — were supposed to work only on the album that just downloaded. A bug meant that when MeedyaDL couldn't confidently identify the album folder up front, these steps fell back to scanning your *whole* output folder instead of just the one album. On a large library, that turned a 30-second job into a 6-minute (or even 25–50 minute) one. This no longer happens — when the specific album can't be pinned down, MeedyaDL now skips the extra step for that item rather than churning through everything you've ever downloaded.
- **Lyrics conversion no longer repeats itself for the same album.** When a download produced files in multiple audio qualities (for example, both Dolby Atmos and a fallback format), the synced-lyrics conversion step used to run once per quality instead of once per album — redoing identical work and adding many extra minutes for no benefit.
- **The library scan used for the above fixes is now capped at a sensible folder depth**, so it can no longer wander unexpectedly deep into unusual folder layouts while trying to locate an album.

### Notes

- Cumulative effect for the library that surfaced this bug: multi-format artist downloads that used to take 25–50 minutes per item now finish in 30–60 seconds.
